doc.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Cooking and turning the barn into a performing space
summary: She cooks like she improvises, plans a performance space in the barn like her Philadelphia Drummers space, and recalls the Urgent Care visit after the fall.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well I love to cook. I cook like a jazz musician, I improvise everything. I watch the Food Network a lot. So I’m always trying to make things I see on the Food Network. So I love doing that. And I have been doing a lot of that.

And thinking about plans for this barn. My place in Philadelphia I had lived in an old stationary factory and we turned the first floor into a performing arts space called Drummers. So this barn, while it’s still in relative, it’s in some chaos, because like I said I’m just getting back on my feet, but this is going to be a performing arts space too. So it’s a whole downstairs area, it was a dairy barn, old stables and stuff and a huge garage and these super cool area in the back that could be a great recording studio or like a colonial pub. And there’s this. I’m actually, I don’t know how well you can see this,

That structure in the back is, I call it the tin can. That’s about a 2200 square foot house that we live in. Here’s the upstairs where there can be a balcony or a second floor. And then you can’t really see the whole thing but anyway, it’s a big barn.

Well so that’s going to be a performing space too, and as soon as we’re allowed to gather I’m going to have a concert here, at least with my trio, because we’re set up to roll with that and invite the whole neighborhood, just for fun.
Well let someone else move the piano, all right?

Yeah. You know when you think about how stupid to fall off of one step. I mean it’s so stupid I can’t even believe it when I think back. It’ so annoying. My right foot got twisted in a blanket, and then of course I’m thinking oh good, there’s a pandemic, everything is closed. So I drove myself to, like I said, it was the day we were moving so the moving trucks were there so Susan couldn’t come with me so I drove myself to Urgent Care which was a brand new one on Girard Street in Philly, and nobody was there and they let me right in and then miraculously this orthopedic place was open. I was very happy I didn’t need surgery.
